High-impact live changes made with an API key or on someone else's behalf queue for the owner's review instead (the owner is notified with a review link). configure_agent_business_rules edits a single named operational-rules section.

business_id.description: Business ID. Required when the agent has multiple accessible assignments.

first_message.description: Spoken greeting / first message callers hear.

inbound_prompt.description: The whole inbound prompt; it replaces the current one. Start from inbound_prompt in get_agent_config, never from a saved version.

voice_catalog_id.description: Preferred way to pick a voice: an id from list_voices.

voice.description: Voice selection: { provider, voiceId }. Use voice_catalog_id instead when you can.

model.description: Language model selection: { provider, model, temperature }.

transfer_phone_number.description: Number to transfer qualified calls to.

call_summary_instructions.description: How the summary written after each call should read, in plain language (for example "Write exactly two sentences for the attorney..."). Changes only the summary; the prompt and scoring stay as they are. get_operational_settings shows the current text.

lead_score_instructions.description: How each caller is scored from 0 to 100, in plain language. Changes only the scoring. End it with "Respond with ONLY a number from 0 to 100."

reason.description: Why this change is being made. Kept in the change history.

idempotency_key.description: Required for writes. Reuse the same key when retrying the same change.

actor.description: Do not set. Kept for older clients; the signed-in connection identifies you.

authority.description: Do not set. It cannot approve a change: the owner approves through review_url or by being signed in.

dry_run.description: Validate and summarize the change without writing.

queue_for_approval.description: When authority is missing, create a pending dashboard approval instead of returning needs_approval.

source_ref.description: External source reference, such as a support ticket or conversation ID.

tools.name: request_emergency_address
tools.title: Set Emergency (911) Address
tools.description: Set the emergency (E911) service address for one of the business's phone numbers with the phone carrier, so a 911 call from that line reaches the right dispatcher. Needs phone_number, the full street address and disclosure_acknowledged true after the owner reads the 911 notice, plus the owner's confirmed approval. Replaces any address on file for that number. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

phone_number.description: The business line, in E.164 format.

customerName.description: Business or person at the address.

disclosure_acknowledged.description: True only after the owner has read and accepted the 911 service notice.

Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.title: Send Kai Into a Meeting
tools.description: Send Kai into a Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex meeting by its link. Kai joins under the agent name, takes notes, and emails the owner a summary when the meeting ends. If the meeting has a waiting room, the host must admit Kai. In the default listen mode it answers out loud when someone says its name and counts against the plan's monthly meeting minutes (a business whose plan includes none gets its first hour free, once); avatar mode joins with a talking video face and counts one avatar meeting.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access several businesses).

meeting_url.description: The meeting link, e.g. https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij or a zoom.us join link.

agent_id.description: Which agent joins (optional; defaults to the business's first agent).

bot_name.description: Name shown in the meeting and the name people say to get a reply (optional; defaults to the agent's name). Must be a short, speakable name.

camera_image_url.description: Public https link to a .jpg shown as the camera tile (optional).

instructions.description: Context for this meeting only, e.g. "This is an onboarding call for a new customer; they need help with setup" (optional, up to 2000 characters).

mode.description: 'listen' (default): joins with a still camera tile and answers out loud when someone says its name. 'avatar': joins with a talking video face; counts as one avatar meeting (separate from meeting minutes; every business gets one free), stays on camera for the first 30 minutes, then continues voice-only and leaves at 60 minutes.

avatar_id.description: Avatar mode only: which stock face to use (optional; an unknown id returns the list of valid ones).

tools.name: get_meeting
tools.title: Get Meetings
tools.description: List the meetings Kai was sent into (newest first), or one meeting by id with its live status, minutes used and summary, plus the plan's remaining meeting minutes this month.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access several businesses).

id.description: Meeting id (optional; omit to list recent meetings).

tools.name: leave_meeting
tools.title: Take Kai Out of a Meeting
tools.description: Have Kai leave a video meeting it is in, or stop trying to join one. Kai drops out of the live call for everyone in it and stops taking notes; this cannot be undone, and joining again takes a new join_meeting request. Notes taken so far are kept and can be read with get_meeting.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access several businesses).

id.description: Meeting id from join_meeting or get_meeting.

annotations.title: Take Kai Out of a Meeting

tools.name: get_usage
tools.title: Get API Usage
tools.description: List recent API usage events (endpoint, method, status code, cost) for the caller's account.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.title: List Plans
tools.description: Read the canonical public KaiCalls plan catalog, monthly USD prices and allowances. Does not select a plan, create checkout, or change billing.

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.title: Get Checkout Status
tools.description: Read a Stripe-verified subscription checkout receipt for a business you own. Requires business_id and session_id from checkout. Confirmed billing does not prove agent, number, or call activation; get_activation_status reports setup proof. This tool never creates checkout or retries provisioning.

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Send Message
tools.description: Send one message to a business's customer on the channel you choose: a text (sms) from one of the business's agent lines, or a WhatsApp message from its connected WhatsApp number. The same consent, Do-Not-Call, quiet-hours and rate gates as the dashboard apply, and a refusal says which one. sms needs from_agent_id; whatsapp needs a number the owner connected to WhatsApp (pass from when there is more than one) and a customer who messaged that number in the last 24 hours. Email is not sent here; draft_email_campaign drafts a campaign the owner reviews and approves. business_id is required when the account has more than one business. The result reports that the provider accepted the message, not that it was delivered.

business_id.description: The business sending. Required when the account has more than one.

from_agent_id.description: sms only (required): the agent whose phone line sends the text.

from.description: whatsapp only: the business's connected WhatsApp number, when it has more than one.

lead_id.description: Optional lead ID to link and honor the lead's automation-pause state.

idempotency_key.description: Optional caller-supplied key. Completed replays return the original send. New keyed WhatsApp requests reserve a durable intent before dispatch. Uncertain or concurrent replays are refused, and a new key is treated as a new send. Legacy lost receipts remain unverified.

tools.name: request_email_sender
tools.title: Request Email Sending Domain
tools.description: Set up a sending address for a business's email campaigns on a domain the business controls (for example mail.example.com). Registers the domain with the email delivery provider and returns the DNS records the owner must add where the domain is hosted. May replace an existing reply address, enabled state and sending limit, and may provision provider inbound routing, inbox and webhook. Sends no email. The sender becomes ready on its own once the records verify; check_email_sender re-checks now. Needs an admin of the business. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

from.description: The From address on that domain.

reply_to.description: Where customer replies go. Must also be an address on that domain.

tools.name: check_email_sender
tools.title: Check Email Sending Domain
tools.description: Re-check a sending domain's DNS records with the email delivery provider now and replace its saved verification proof; may finish provider inbound routing, inbox and webhook setup. Returns what is still missing; an empty list means the sender is ready. Sends no email. Any member of the business may check.

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

sender_id.description: The sender to re-check, from request_email_sender or get_email_campaign.

tools.name: record_email_consent
tools.title: Record Email Permission
tools.description: Record that existing customers gave the business permission to email them, with evidence_ref saying where that permission came from. Pass lead_id and email for one customer, or emails for up to 200. Addresses that are not existing customers are skipped and listed. Sends no email. Needs an admin of the business. Each record states that the owner holds that permission.

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

lead_id.description: One existing customer (lead id), paired with email.

emails.description: Email addresses of existing customers, up to 200, as an alternative to lead_id.

evidence_ref.description: Where the permission came from or why it is withdrawn, e.g. 'web form opt-in' or 'customer asked to stop'.

expires_at.description: Optional: when the permission ends (ISO date).

tools.name: revoke_email_consent
tools.title: Revoke Email Permission
tools.description: Take back email permission for existing customers so no campaign can email them. Pass lead_id and email for one customer, or emails for up to 200, with evidence_ref saying why. Needs an admin of the business.

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

lead_id.description: One existing customer (lead id), paired with email.

emails.description: Email addresses of existing customers, up to 200, as an alternative to lead_id.

evidence_ref.description: Where the permission came from or why it is withdrawn, e.g. 'web form opt-in' or 'customer asked to stop'.

tools.name: draft_email_campaign
tools.title: Draft Email Campaign
tools.description: Save an email campaign for the business to review: a subject, a plain-text body, the customers to email (lead_ids, each with recorded email permission) and who it comes from: a verified sending domain (sender_id) or one of the business's own connected email accounts (email_account_id, listed under emailAccounts by get_email_campaign; sends at most 100 a day and 20 an hour, spaced out). Each customer gets their own email, addressed to them alone. Returns the campaign id and the fingerprint of this exact revision. Sends nothing; an owner or admin approves it with approve_email_campaign and it only goes out after launch_email_campaign. subject and text may use {{ first_name }}, {{ last_order_date }} and {{ last_order_items }} (filled per customer from the connected booking system; order_window picks which booking) or any key in lead_variables. Needs an admin of the business. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

sender_id.description: The verified sending domain to send from. Pass this or email_account_id.

email_account_id.description: One of the business's own connected email accounts to send from (its id from get_email_campaign emailAccounts). Pass this or sender_id.

lead_ids.description: The customers (lead ids) to email; each needs recorded email permission.

lead_variables.description: Optional per-customer values for placeholders in subject/text, keyed by lead id: {"<lead_id>": {"last_order_date": "Nov 22, 2025"}}. {{ first_name }} is filled from the contact name unless given here; {{ key | default: "there" }} sets a fallback. Each customer gets their own email.

order_window.description: Optional: which booking fills {{ last_order_date }} and {{ last_order_items }}. A holiday week ({"holiday": "thanksgiving", "year": 2025}; year defaults to last year) or dates ({"start": "2025-11-24", "end": "2025-11-30"}). Without it, each customer's most recent past booking is used.

daily_limit.description: Optional: most emails sent per day (default: the most the sender and the Kai level allow).

design.description: Optional structured email design. text must equal its rendered text version; no raw HTML. The owner approves the exact HTML and text.

tools.name: approve_email_campaign
tools.title: Approve Email Campaign
tools.description: An owner or admin of the business approves one exact revision of a drafted email campaign, named by campaign_id and the fingerprint returned by draft_email_campaign or get_email_campaign. A changed draft has a new fingerprint and needs a new approval. Sends nothing; launch_email_campaign queues it. Needs an owner or admin of the business.

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the exact revision the owner reviewed.

tools.name: launch_email_campaign
tools.title: Launch Email Campaign
tools.description: Queue an approved email campaign for sending to real customers, within its daily limit. Needs an owner or admin of the business. Emails cannot be unsent once delivered; cancel_email_campaign stops what has not gone out yet. A queued result is not proof any email was delivered. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

tools.name: cancel_email_campaign
tools.title: Cancel Email Campaign
tools.description: Stop an email campaign so nothing more is sent from it. Emails already delivered stay delivered. Needs campaign_id and the fingerprint of its current revision. Needs an owner or admin of the business.

business_id.description: The business that sends the email.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of its current revision, from get_email_campaign.

tools.name: get_email_campaign
tools.title: Get Email Campaign
tools.description: Read a business's email campaigns: its sending addresses and their setup readiness, recent campaigns with status, revision fingerprint and outcome counts, and the customers who can be emailed (recorded consent, not on the do-not-email list). Pass campaign_id for one campaign, or sender_id for the DNS records that sending address's domain needs. Read-only; any member of the business can read.

sender_id.description: Optional: that sender's domain setup records instead of the campaign view.

tools.name: find_rebook_customers
tools.title: Find Customers To Rebook
tools.description: List a business's customers who booked a week last year (for example Thanksgiving week) and have not booked the same week this year, biggest last-year spend first, from the orders in the business's connected booking system. Each row has the customer's name and company, a masked phone, whether there is an email, and last year's order numbers, dates and totals. Returns email_ready_lead_ids (recorded email permission, not on the do-not-email list) to pass straight to draft_email_campaign, and call_list (name, phone, last-year total) for staff to dial by hand: Kai never calls or texts these past customers. Customers whose details have not been looked up yet show contact 'not_looked_up'; prepare_rebook_customers fills them in. Read-only; needs a connected booking system.

business_id.description: Required when the account has more than one business.

holiday.description: Compare this holiday's week last year with the same week this year (Monday to Sunday around the holiday; Memorial Day and Labor Day take the seven days ending on the holiday; new-years is the week of New Year's Eve). Use this or this_year_start/this_year_end.

year.description: Optional with holiday: the year to fill (default: this year). Last year's week is the year before.

this_year_start.description: Optional instead of holiday: first day, YYYY-MM-DD.

this_year_end.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, at most 92 days).

last_year_start.description: Optional: first day of the earlier range. Default: the same weekdays 52 weeks before.

last_year_end.description: Optional: last day of the earlier range.

tools.name: prepare_rebook_customers
tools.title: Prepare Customers To Rebook
tools.description: For the customers find_rebook_customers lists as 'not_looked_up', read their name, phone and email from the business's booking system and save them as past customers, so the list can be emailed and called. Past customers raise no new-lead alerts and are never put in Kai call or text campaigns. Reads a few customers a minute (the booking system's limit), so one call may not finish: when remaining is above 0, call again. A customer that cannot be read stays on the list. Sends nothing. Requires an admin of the business.

business_id.description: Required when the account has more than one business.

holiday.description: Compare this holiday's week last year with the same week this year (Monday to Sunday around the holiday; Memorial Day and Labor Day take the seven days ending on the holiday; new-years is the week of New Year's Eve). Use this or this_year_start/this_year_end.

year.description: Optional with holiday: the year to fill (default: this year). Last year's week is the year before.

this_year_start.description: Optional instead of holiday: first day, YYYY-MM-DD.

this_year_end.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, at most 92 days).

last_year_start.description: Optional: first day of the earlier range. Default: the same weekdays 52 weeks before.

last_year_end.description: Optional: last day of the earlier range.

tools.name: set_conversation_owner
tools.title: Set Conversation Owner
tools.description: Set who answers a customer's text conversation. owner 'ai' (the default): Kai replies. 'human': Kai stays quiet and the business owner answers. 'external': Kai stays quiet and the business's own system answers; it receives the sms.received webhook and replies with send_message or POST /v1/messages. With external_reply_timeout_seconds (external only, 60 to 86400), Kai answers a message nothing replied to in that time. Messages are always stored and sms.received always fires. Pass conversation_id for one conversation, or phone for every conversation the business has with that customer. Re-sending the same owner changes nothing.

conversation_id.description: One conversation. Either this or phone is required.

phone.description: The customer's number (E.164): every conversation the business has with it.

business_id.description: Required when the account has more than one business and only phone is given.

external_reply_timeout_seconds.description: owner 'external' only: Kai answers when nothing replied in this many seconds.

tools.name: get_business_verification
tools.title: Get Business Verification Documents
tools.description: Read tenant-scoped business-verification document references, pending/approved/rejected staff-review states and secure upload requirements. No file bytes, storage paths, signed URLs or tax identifiers. Uploads happen on the secure owner page, by an admin; rejected documents can be corrected and uploaded again. Internal staff verification is separate from carrier registration. Reviewer notes are returned as staff-written data.

tools.name: submit_text_registration
tools.title: Text Registration Submission Availability
tools.description: Reserved submission contract; execution is currently unavailable and returns submission_unavailable without filing. Shared durable reservation and unknown-outcome reconciliation across dashboard, checkout and cron are prerequisites. Preparation and status are handled by get_text_registration and save_text_registration_details. Saving corrected details does not resubmit existing rejected provider objects: operator reconciliation is required. Another entry point or a new paid registration would duplicate the filing. It accepts no tax identifiers, credentials, file contents or legal attestations. Owner membership and billing:write required.

tools.name: get_consent_proof
tools.title: Get Consent Proof
tools.description: Read the consent proof for one phone number at a business: for service texts, marketing texts, calls and WhatsApp, the current status, when consent was given or taken back, how (web form, keyword, call, manual, API), the exact wording shown, and the stored proof (form page, form time, submission id), plus up to 50 history entries, newest first. Use it to answer a carrier or customer asking how someone opted in. IP addresses are never returned. found false means no consent record exists for that number. Read-only.

tools.name: get_text_registration
tools.title: Get Text Registration
tools.description: Read where a business stands on its own carrier registration for business texting: saved details (never the EIN; only whether one is on file), payment, filing stage, whether sales texts are allowed, and the one next step. In MCP, `known` excludes fields the canonical flow still requires the owner to confirm; `suggestions` preserves those nonprivate values and available provenance. `missing` is the ordered outstanding field-question list, with missing_value or confirmation_required reasons; `next_question` is its first item. `question_progress` counts field questions including next, not website screens. Website screens group several fields and may include a private identity step; unequal counts can be valid. The MCP presentation separates configured registration/enrollment from recipient-specific sending permission and delivery, which remain not_checked. A null own registration does not prove an enrolled platform route cannot text; configured lines do not prove a send is authorized. Dashboard/API presentation is unchanged. Pass check=true to also run the pre-filing check: every problem a carrier reviewer would reject the registration on (business details, campaign wording, website, privacy policy, texting terms, opt-in page), each as `prefiling_check.items` with a plain fix, so it can be fixed before anything is paid. Read-only.

check.description: Also run the pre-filing check and return prefiling_check (ready, items with title and fix).

tools.name: save_text_registration_details
tools.title: Save Text Registration Details
tools.description: Save a business's legal name, the name customers know it by (if different), entity type, industry, website, address, authorized contact and what it will text (service only, or service and sales) for its own carrier registration. Business owner, or an admin of the business (such as the partner that created the workspace) preparing it for the owner. Each field holds an answer from the owner; anything omitted is filled from what is already on file (see get_text_registration `known`). Answers can be saved one at a time: answers given so far are kept, and while questions remain the result lists `saved_steps`, `missing` and `next_question`. The owner can finish here or on the registration page. Never takes the EIN: the owner types it on the registration page returned as setup_url. Each saved answer replaces the value on file for that field. Refused once a filing is already with the carriers. Charges nothing and files nothing.

legal_business_name.description: Exactly as on the IRS EIN letter.

brand_name.description: Optional: the name customers know the business by, when it differs from the legal name (a DBA or trade name, as shown on its website). Texts are signed with it.

street.description: Must match the address the IRS has.

contact_phone.description: A US number the carriers can reach.

contact_title.description: As the contact signs, e.g. Owner.

text_types.description: service: replies and follow-ups to people who contacted the business. service_and_sales: also lets sales texts go to people who opted in to marketing.

tools.name: start_text_registration_checkout
tools.title: Start Text Registration Checkout
tools.description: Create the payment link for a business's own carrier registration (a one-time filing fee plus a monthly campaign fee). Business owner only, and only once the details and the EIN are saved. An admin who prepared the details gets owner_required with owner_handoff_url: the page the owner opens to type the EIN, review and confirm. Returns checkout_url for the owner to open and pay; nothing is charged by this tool, and filing starts only after payment. A checkout_url means neither payment nor filing. On a plan that includes registration there is nothing to pay: the tool sends it to the carriers straight away and returns included_in_plan and filed true instead of a link, so that path requires confirm_submission true, which records that the owner reviewed and confirmed the saved details and external submission. Submission is not carrier approval. The tool takes no EIN, document contents, credentials or legal attestations.

confirm_submission.description: True only after the owner explicitly confirms the saved details and possible immediate carrier submission.

tools.name: set_branded_caller_id
tools.title: Set Branded Caller ID
tools.description: File the business name that landlines show when the business's number calls out (caller ID name). Included with the business's own text registration once it is paid; charges nothing. Business owner only. The name must be at most 15 characters, start with a letter, and use only letters, numbers, periods, commas and spaces (get_text_registration returns a suggestion in branded_caller_id.suggestedName). Files with the carriers once the business profile is approved; review then takes a day or two and carriers show it within 72 hours. US local numbers only. The result confirms the filing, not that the name is showing on calls.

display_name.description: Up to 15 characters, e.g. SUMMIT ROOFING.

tools.name: start_own_caller_id
tools.title: Start Own Caller ID
tools.description: Let Kai's outbound calls show a number the person already owns (their cell or an old main line) instead of a KaiCalls line, so people recognize who is calling. A verification call goes to that number and returns a code; the person answers and types the code on the keypad. Then get_own_caller_id confirms it. Ownership is proven only by that call. US and Canada numbers. Business owner only. Charges nothing. Callbacks to the shown number reach that phone, not Kai. use_by_default (default true) shows it on every call unless make_call asks for caller_id 'business_line'. Starting a new number replaces the old one.

phone_number.description: The number to show, e.g. +19085551234. It must ring a phone the person can answer.

use_by_default.description: Show it on every call unless a call asks otherwise (optional, default true).

tools.name: get_own_caller_id
tools.title: Get Own Caller ID
tools.description: Which number Kai's outbound calls show: the person's own verified number or the KaiCalls line. Also confirms a verification started with start_own_caller_id once the person has typed the code. state is none, pending, verified or failed.

tools.name: remove_own_caller_id
tools.title: Remove Own Caller ID
tools.description: Stop showing the person's own number on Kai's calls; calls show the KaiCalls line again. Business owner only.

tools.name: create_customer_workspace
tools.title: Create Customer Workspace
tools.description: Create a new KaiCalls account for a business, owned by the business owner's own email address. It lets a partner or helper set up KaiCalls for a business owner. The account starts without a plan or phone number: the result includes a link the owner opens themselves to choose a plan and add their card, and the line is set up only after they pay. This tool charges nothing. By default the caller is added as an admin of the new account so they can continue setup (get_setup_checklist lists the steps); join_as_admin false skips that. partner_code credits a referring partner and does not apply to a partner's own account. Fails, creating nothing, if the email already has a KaiCalls account.

owner_email.description: The business owner's own email. They own the workspace.

owner_cell.description: Owner's cell; calls ring it first once the line is live.

partner_linked.description: Present for a partner-scoped key: the new business is linked to the partner.

tools.name: set_up_business
tools.title: Customize Business Line
tools.description: Optional line customization: sets the business name and greeting Kai answers with, as the owner requested. Not required to make calls, and never changes payment, usage or fraud limits. Extra business details are optional; no business-qualification questionnaire is needed. An existing business greeting is left unchanged.

business_id.description: The account to set up. Optional when the token reaches one account.

what_you_sell.description: What the business sells or does, in the owner's words.

website.description: The business's website, if it has one.

who_kai_will_call.description: Who the owner wants Kai to call, e.g. other businesses, existing customers, or people who asked for a callback.

tools.name: get_setup_checklist
tools.title: Get Setup Checklist
tools.description: Read where one business stands on setup: plan, phone number, texting registration, WhatsApp, call and lead alerts, connected mailbox for follow-up email, and email campaign sender. Each step has a state (done, in_progress, needs_owner, needs_action or unavailable) and one next action: either the tool that moves it forward, or the page the owner must open for steps only they can do, such as paying, typing their EIN or signing in to Facebook or Google. Read-only; changes nothing and contacts no one.

business_id.description: The business to check.

tools.name: connect_whatsapp
tools.title: Connect WhatsApp
tools.description: Get the one link a business owner opens to put WhatsApp on their KaiCalls number. They sign in to Facebook as an admin of the business's Meta Business account and verify the number; the business owns its WhatsApp account. Uses the business's oldest KaiCalls line unless phone_number names another of its lines. Returns the same link while it is still valid (up to 3 days). Owner or admin only. Creates nothing billable and connects nothing by itself: get_whatsapp_status reports the connection after the owner finishes, and WhatsApp is not connected until it says so.

phone_number.description: E.164, one of the business lines.

tools.name: get_whatsapp_status
tools.title: Get WhatsApp Status
tools.description: Check whether WhatsApp is connected on a business's KaiCalls number, read live from the carrier. Connected only once the number is verified for WhatsApp; otherwise says whether the owner's link is still waiting, expired or failed.

tools.name: get_channel_status
tools.title: Get Channel Status
tools.description: Read customer channel setup. Phone calls report configured number resources only: state configured or needs_setup, with canSend/canReceive null because operational availability is unknown. SMS has state not_checked and null send/receive flags; shared_setup_state retains the existing configuration summary, not recipient-specific permission. Registration detail requires billing:read; this SMS-scope summary reads no new billing details. Other channels retain their existing states and flags. private_test_readiness checks owner-private call setup only when the token also has agents:read; otherwise it is not_checked with reconnect scope guidance. Private testing does not establish customer coverage or outbound call permission, which remain not_checked. Email includes separate managedEmail campaign sender readiness; a connected mailbox does not prove campaign approval or delivery. Read-only; changes nothing.

tools.name: get_trust_level
tools.title: Get Trust Level
tools.description: Read one business's KaiCalls trust level (Sprout, Verified, Trusted, Pro, Partner): the current level, the steps to the next one with progress, what each level unlocks, today's outbound calls and texts against current effective account limits, and any hold. Badge progress does not itself establish higher call or text caps. focus 'ladder' explains every level; focus 'level' with level explains one. Read-only: returns saved standing or computes missing/stale standing without saving it or sending notifications. recheck_trust_level recomputes and saves current standing. Levels are earned, never set: no tool can raise one.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token reaches exactly one business).

focus.description: 'standing' (default): the current level and next steps. 'ladder': every level. 'level': the one named in level. 'outbound': today's outbound calls and texts against the limits this level allows, and the step that raises them.

level.description: A level key or name, e.g. 'pro'. Used with focus 'level'.

tools.name: recheck_trust_level
tools.title: Recheck Trust Level
tools.description: Recompute one business's KaiCalls trust level now from its live account activity (card on file, paid bills, days active, real customer calls) and save the result, the same recheck the dashboard runs, for example right after the owner adds a card. Returns the same view as get_trust_level plus whether the level moved up or down. Requires current business membership. Replaces the saved derived state, may record level-change history and may email the current owner when standing changes. It can only reflect what the account has earned; it never sets or raises a level by request.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token reaches exactly one business).

focus.description: 'standing' (default): the current level and next steps. 'ladder': every level. 'level': the one named in level. 'outbound': today's outbound calls and texts against the limits this level allows, and the step that raises them.

level.description: A level key or name, e.g. 'pro'. Used with focus 'level'.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.title: Get Balance
tools.description: Get plan terms and usage for accessible businesses. No-card trials report 25 lifetime minutes, zero price and no overage; paid plans report the mapped subscription price and billing-cycle usage. Answered-call allowance usage is the raw billable call count, matching dashboard and right-sizing. A separate weighted count is informational only, not allowance consumption or right-sizing. Phone allowance includes purchased extra lines. A balance does not prove activation or inbound routing. Unavailable billing data returns an error.

price_monthly.description: Mapped subscription base price in USD; zero for no-card trial. Excludes add-ons and tax.

answered_calls_used.description: Raw billable call count used for allowance reporting, matching dashboard and right-sizing; null for minute plans.

answered_calls_raw.description: Unweighted billable call count for reporting.

answered_calls_weighted.description: Informational only, not allowance consumption or right-sizing: ordinary calls 1, human-answered silent-listen calls 0.5; null for minute plans.

phone_numbers.description: Active registered numbers, including unassigned numbers.

period_end.description: Null for lifetime trial usage; does not imply the trial cannot expire.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.title: Create or Resume Checkout
tools.description: Create, or reuse, a secure payment page hosted by Stripe where the business owner pays for a KaiCalls plan from list_plans with their own card. Needs business_id, plan_id and an idempotency_key: retrying with the same key returns the same page, and choosing a different plan needs a new key. This tool charges nothing; only the owner can pay, by opening the page themselves. It never proves payment or that the phone line is live: get_checkout_status reports payment for the returned session_id.

business_id.description: The business the plan is for.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for this checkout; reuse it when retrying.

tools.name: list_numbers
tools.title: List Phone Numbers
tools.description: List phone numbers assigned to the accessible business(es), with capability and compliance flags. Assignment does not prove a successful inbound test or customer coverage. get_activation_status reports current readiness and private-test proof. Forwarding is an optional customer route.

business_id.description: Business ID to filter by (optional).

tools.name: get_phone_flow
tools.title: Get Phone Flow
tools.description: Read how calls ring on the business's hosted phone system: which cells and desk phones ring, for how many seconds, and whether after-hours callers go straight to Kai. Reconciled from the phone system on every call. Returns 409 when the hosted phone system is not set up for this business.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access multiple businesses).

tools.name: update_phone_flow
tools.title: Update Phone Flow
tools.description: Replace how calls ring on the business's hosted phone system with a full phone flow: { version: 1, hours: { mode: 'always' | 'business_hours', afterHours: 'kai' }, ring: { members: [{ kind: 'cell', phone: E.164, label, requirePressOne } | { kind: 'desk_phone' | 'user', userId, label }], timeoutSeconds: 5-120 }, overflow: 'kai' }. Applied idempotently (only real differences are written); every member passes the forwarding-loop guard; business_hours mode derives the schedule from the business hours already on file. Because it replaces the whole flow, the input is the full flow as get_phone_flow returns it, with changes applied.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access multiple businesses).

flow.description: The complete phone flow to apply.

tools.name: set_up_phone_system
tools.title: Set Up Phone System
tools.description: Turn the business's number into a hosted phone system: Kai is installed as extension 700, the owner's mobile joins the list of phones to ring first, and calls reach Kai when nobody picks up. Idempotent and resumable — a re-run reuses everything already created and reports it under `reused`. Needs a complete US street address on file (the emergency-services and tax location) and the owner's mobile: when either is missing the tool fails with `code` missing_address or missing_owner_mobile plus `required_field` and `next_action` naming exactly what is missing, which business_address or owner_mobile accepts. Returns the status shape (existing setup IDs, extension and the phone-system line) and `next_step`, the owner's next action in one line (forward your line here / dial 700 from any office phone).

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access multiple businesses).

owner_mobile.description: The owner's own mobile number (US). Optional when set_owner_phone already saved one; required when the last attempt returned missing_owner_mobile.

business_address.description: The business street address to save before provisioning. Optional when a complete address is already on file; required when the last attempt returned missing_address.

persona.description: Which phones the business runs on, if the owner said: cell_only (just the owner's cell) or office (desk phones / an existing office line that will forward in). Shapes next_step; optional.

line.description: The phone-system line (E.164), if a number is attached.

next_step.description: The one line to relay to the owner.

required_field.description: Present when setup is blocked on a missing input.

next_action.description: What to collect and how to retry, when blocked.

issues.description: Address fields to correct when code is invalid_address.

tools.name: get_phone_system_status
tools.title: Get Phone System Status
tools.description: Read saved phone-system configuration: extension, resource IDs (never secrets), assigned line, and agreement. phone_system_configuration.configuration_allows_calls means provisioned resources plus a permitting agreement only; it does not verify calls can connect. ready_for_calls is null because operational availability is unknown. private_test_readiness uses the existing owner-private call setup authority only with agents:read; otherwise not_checked. Customer coverage and outbound call permission remain not_checked. This read differs from the shared phone-system API configuration flag and changes nothing.

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access multiple businesses).

tools.name: add_team_phone
tools.title: Add Team Phone
tools.description: Add a teammate's (or the owner's) cell to the phones that ring before Kai answers. Idempotent — a cell already listed is reported as already included. Owners and admins are also registered on the admin roster, so calling the business line from that cell reaches the admin secretary; a member only rings. The business's own forwarded-from office line is refused (forwarding_loop) because ringing it would bounce the call straight back. Requires the phone system to be set up first (set_up_phone_system).

business_id.description: Business ID (required when the token can access multiple businesses).

phone_number.description: The cell to add, US format (e.g. (908) 555-1234 or +19085551234).

role.description: member only rings; owner and admin also get admin-secretary access from this cell. Defaults to admin.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.title: List SMS Conversations
tools.description: List SMS conversation threads (counterparty timeline metadata) for the authenticated business, most recent first.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.title: Get SMS Conversation
tools.description: Get a single SMS conversation thread by ID.

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.title: Get Webhook Configuration
tools.description: List the configured outbound webhook(s) for a business, including supported event types.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: set_webhook
tools.title: Set Webhook
tools.description: Create or update a business outbound webhook (URL + subscribed events). Returns a webhook secret on first creation only.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

webhook_url.description: HTTPS/HTTP destination URL for event delivery.

id.description: Existing webhook ID to update (omit to create new).

events.description: Event types to subscribe to (get_webhook lists the supported types).

preset.description: Start the body from a CRM field map. Presets are editable starting points, not exact vendor formats. Ignored when payload_template is also sent.

payload_template.description: Shape the body for a CRM: { "fields": { "<their field>": "<path>" | { "value": <fixed> } } }. A path reads the standard event body (e.g. "data.phone", "occurred_at"); "a|b" takes the first with a value; a dot in the field name nests it ("contact.phone"). Missing paths send null. null restores the standard body.

custom_headers.description: Extra headers the CRM needs, as { "Header-Name": "value" } (max 20). A null value keeps the saved value for that name. Content-Type, Host, Content-Length and X-KaiCalls-* cannot be set. Values are never returned.

body_format.description: json (default) or form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, nested keys flattened with dots).

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.title: Delete Webhook
tools.description: Remove a business outbound webhook by ID.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: list_evals
tools.title: List Agent Evals
tools.description: List saved test scenarios for an agent (or all accessible agents). A new agent has none; create_eval adds one.

tools.name: create_eval
tools.title: Create Agent Test Scenario
tools.description: Save a test scenario for one of the business's agents: what a caller says and what the agent's reply must do to pass. run_eval then grades the agent against it. Saving places no call and changes nothing on the agent.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

name.description: Short scenario name, up to 80 characters.

caller_says.description: The caller's opening message, e.g. "I was rear-ended yesterday and need a lawyer."

pass_if.description: What the agent's reply must do to pass, in plain words, e.g. "Asks for the caller's name and number and does not give legal advice."

tools.name: run_eval
tools.title: Run Agent Eval
tools.description: Run a saved test scenario against one of the business's agents and grade the agent's replies: pass eval_id for one scenario, or agent_id for every scenario saved for that agent (see list_evals). The test is a simulated text conversation with the agent's current live configuration; no phone call is placed, no customer is contacted and the agent's configuration is not changed. Each run uses paid voice-agent provider capacity and is recorded with its result, so scenarios already run on the agent's current configuration are not run again unless force is true, and each agent has a daily limit on runs. Returns pass or fail per scenario with the grader's reasons.

eval_id.description: Run this one saved scenario (from list_evals). Either this or agent_id is required.

agent_id.description: Run every saved scenario for this agent. Either this or eval_id is required.

wait.description: Wait for the grade before returning (default true).

max_wait_ms.description: Per-run wait cap in ms when wait is true (default 60000, max 110000).

force.description: Run again even though nothing changed on the agent or these scenarios since they last ran (otherwise refused, since the result would be the same).

tools.name: find_voices
tools.title: Find Voices for an Agent
tools.description: Find the three voices that best match a plain description of what the owner wants (for example 'a Southern man who can also speak Spanish' or 'warm older woman, calm'), and get a page link where the owner can play each one in English and Spanish, pick one to switch the agent's voice, and undo within 24 hours. Show the owner the page link; nothing changes until they pick. The link expires in 7 days.

agent_id.description: The agent whose voice the owner wants to change.

description.description: The owner's own words for the voice: gender, accent or region, age, feel, languages.

business_id.description: Business ID, needed only when the agent belongs to more than one business.

locale.description: Optional language hint like "es" when the description does not say.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.title: List Voice Catalog
tools.description: List the curated, credential-free voice catalog (id, display name, accent, language, gender, sample URL) used to configure agent voices.

language.description: Filter by language label, e.g. English or Spanish.

provider.description: Filter by a voice provider id exactly as list_voices returns it.

gender.description: Filter by gender: male or female.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.title: Create Agent
tools.description: Create a new KaiCalls agent — the secretary that answers this business’s calls (the live voice agent plus KaiCalls records) — with a system prompt, greeting, voice, and model. Its starting settings are saved as version 1 and each later change as a new version (list_config_versions); rollback_config restores a version's greeting, voice, prompt, model and summary/scoring. Compliance: KaiCalls automatically applies state-aware AI-disclosure and consent handling to every agent it provisions, and flags high-risk business categories for extra review.

business_id.description: Business ID to create the agent under.

system_prompt.description: The agent's inbound system prompt (optional). Leave it out to start on the business's industry intake script, the same one a signup gets.

first_message.description: Spoken greeting (optional). Leave it out to use the industry intake greeting, which opens on the caller's need.

vertical_pack.description: Setup pack id (optional; inferred from the business when left out). One of: hvac, plumbing, electrical, general-contractor, garage-door, general-contractors, handyman, landscaping, moving, pest-control, pool-service, cleaning, roofing, personal-injury, family-law, insurance-claims, criminal-defense, eviction-law, legal-family-law, immigration-law, legal-personal-injury, party-rentals, tent-rentals, event-equipment, equipment-rental, restaurant-orders, catering, auto-repair, mobile-mechanic, towing, dive-shop, fitness, wellness-recovery, chiropractic-pt, chiropractic, dental, medical-practice, med-spa, mental-health-therapy, veterinary, photography, salon-barbershop, financial-services, insurance-agency, recruiting-staffing, tax-accounting, property-management, real-estate.

voice_catalog_id.description: Preferred: a curated catalog id from list_voices (optional).

model.description: Language model selection: { provider, model, temperature } (optional).

tools.name: attach_number
tools.title: Attach Phone Number
tools.description: Assign a phone number already in the KaiCalls registry pool to a business (and optionally route it directly to an agent). Does NOT purchase a new number; search_available_numbers and buy_number handle purchases.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

phone_number.description: E.164 phone number already in the registry.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to route this number to directly (optional).

tools.name: attach_own_twilio_number
tools.title: Answer A Number From Your Own Twilio Account
tools.description: Have a voice agent answer calls on ONE number from the business's own connected Twilio account, calls only. Reads only that number. dry_run defaults to true and changes nothing: it returns would_change (the number's VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod) and the fields left unchanged. With dry_run false, only that number's VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod change; its text settings (SmsUrl, SmsMethod, SmsApplicationSid, StatusCallback) are read back afterwards and must be unchanged, so a texting setup another service runs on the account keeps working. Refuses a number a Twilio app answers, and a number another service answers unless replace_existing_voice is true. Uses one plan line. Requires admin role.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

phone_number.description: E.164 number on the business's own connected Twilio account.

agent_id.description: Agent that should answer the calls.

dry_run.description: Default true: report what would change and write nothing.

replace_existing_voice.description: Allow replacing another service that answers calls on this number today.

annotations.title: Answer A Number From Your Own Twilio Account

tools.name: detach_own_twilio_number
tools.title: Stop Answering A Number From Your Own Twilio Account
tools.description: Stop a voice agent answering a number from the business's own connected Twilio account and put back the call setting (VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod) the number had before it was attached. The number is never released from the account and its text settings are not touched. Requires admin role.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

annotations.title: Stop Answering A Number From Your Own Twilio Account

tools.name: set_owner_phone
tools.title: Set Owner Phone
tools.description: Saves the owner's own mobile number on the business record (the number Kai texts whenever it takes a call for the owner) so Kai can ring it first and so activation/forwarding follow-ups can reach a human — connecting a number alone does not prove the owner can be reached. In the acquisition flow this step comes before search_available_numbers and buy_number (#2086). US numbers only; normalized to E.164 and rejected if it cannot be validated as a US mobile/landline number. When ring_first is true (default), also configures ring-first routing so calls hit this cell before overflowing to the secretary — the same path used at signup. declined=true, in place of owner_phone, records a caller who declines to give a number as an inquiry: a KaiCalls lead, with no provisioned business or number.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

owner_phone.description: The owner's own mobile number, US format (e.g. (908) 555-1234 or +19085551234). Required unless declined is true.

ring_first.description: When true (default), ring this number first and overflow to the secretary. When false, only saves the number.

declined.description: True (in place of owner_phone) when the caller will not give a reachable number. Records the business as an inquiry lead instead of a provisioned number.

contact_name.description: Only used with declined=true: the caller name, for the inquiry record.

contact_email.description: Only used with declined=true: an email for the inquiry record, if given.

tools.name: detach_number
tools.title: Detach Phone Number
tools.description: Release a phone number from a business back to the unassigned registry pool.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: search_available_numbers
tools.title: Search Available Numbers
tools.description: Search the carrier for phone numbers available to purchase (live number inventory). In the acquisition flow this follows set_owner_phone, which saves a reachable owner number or records a decline.

business_id.description: Search that business's carrier inventory (optional; defaults to the platform carrier).

tools.name: buy_number
tools.title: Buy Phone Number
tools.description: Request a real phone-number purchase. This is APPROVAL-GATED: the carrier bills immediately on execution, so the tool only prepares a request for authenticated owner review. Caller-supplied human_confirmed, dashboard_session, or system_policy fields never authorize execution. Returns the stored request and a review URL for the owner; while approval is pending, no number has been purchased. Existing entitlement and carrier reservation checks still apply. In the acquisition flow this follows set_owner_phone, which saves a reachable owner number or records a decline.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

phone_number.description: The exact E.164 phone number to purchase, as returned by search_available_numbers.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to route this number to directly once purchased (optional; requires the number to also be voice-runtime-imported, which is not guaranteed at purchase time — a follow-up attach_number call routes it reliably).

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for the purchase request; repeating it returns the original outcome. Defaults to a key derived from the phone number — a new key retries a previously failed purchase.

actor.description: Who is asking: { type: agent|human|system|integration, id, display_name }.

authority.description: Attribution only. human_confirmed and other caller-supplied modes cannot authorize a purchase. Authenticated owner review of the exact stored request is required.

queue_for_approval.description: Create a durable owner-review request (default true). Setting false returns needs_approval, but an authority-envelope retry still cannot execute.

dry_run.description: Validate tenant, scope, and policy without buying anything.

reason.description: Optional reason recorded in the durable audit.

source_ref.description: External source reference, such as a ticket or automation run ID.

result.description: On executed: { number, voice_agent_registered, agent_attached, compliance: { high_risk_category, disclosure_note } }.

tools.name: list_knowledge
tools.title: List Agent Knowledge
tools.description: List agent knowledge base entries for a business.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: upsert_knowledge
tools.title: Create or Update Agent Knowledge
tools.description: Create a new agent knowledge base entry, or update one when `id` is provided. Creating requires title, content, and content_type.

id.description: Knowledge item ID to update (omit to create).

business_id.description: Business ID. Required for create when the token can access multiple businesses.

tools.name: list_products
tools.title: List Agent Products
tools.description: List a business's agent product catalog.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

inventory.description: Include current inventory quantity per product (optional).

tools.name: upsert_product
tools.title: Create or Update Agent Product
tools.description: Create a new product row, or update one when `id` is provided. Creating requires name and business_id. Pass `quantity` to set/update inventory.

id.description: Product ID to update (omit to create).

business_id.description: Business ID. Required for create when the token can access multiple businesses.

image_url.description: Public https photo of the product. Shown next to it when the agent lists options on a caller's screen. Null clears it.

tools.name: get_agent_config
tools.title: Get Agent Configuration
tools.description: Read an agent's settings as the owner edits them: the editable inbound, outbound and text prompts, greeting, voice (with its list_voices id when it has one), model, call length, transfer settings, and the call summary and lead score instructions. Read this before update_agent_config: inbound_prompt there replaces the whole prompt, so edit the text returned here.

business_id.description: Business ID. Needed only when the agent belongs to more than one.

tools.name: list_config_versions
tools.title: List Agent Config Versions
tools.description: List the saved versions of an agent's settings, newest first: what saved each one (source), what changed (diff_summary), who (created_by) and which version a rollback came from. Secrets are never included. Pass `version` to fetch one version's full saved settings (config_snapshot). That snapshot holds the compiled prompt; to edit the prompt, read get_agent_config instead.

version.description: Fetch a single version by its per-agent version_number, including its redacted config_snapshot (optional; omit to list).

limit.description: Max versions to return when listing (optional, default 50, max 100).

tools.name: get_change_history
tools.title: Get Agent Change History
tools.description: List an agent's recent config-change audit trail (change_type, change_source, old/new value, timestamp) — the same change log the owner hears when they call their line and ask what changed. Every change KaiCalls makes to an agent (via update_agent_config, configure_agent_business_rules, the owner's call-in line, or the dashboard) is logged here. Rows carry no version number; to undo a change, pick a version from list_config_versions and use rollback_config.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to fetch change history for.

tools.name: rollback_config
tools.title: Rollback Agent Configuration
tools.description: Request a rollback to a saved version of the agent settings. It restores the version's greeting, voice, prompt (and the editable prompt copy, when the version saved one), model and call summary/scoring. Transfer settings, call length, tools and speech recognition stay as they are; the result lists what was and was not restored. When the business owner or an admin is signed in through this connector, the rollback applies immediately; otherwise the owner approves it from a review link. Targets are listed by list_config_versions. The rollback is itself saved as a new version, and secrets are never copied.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

version_number.description: Version number to restore, from list_config_versions. One of version_number/version_id is required.

version_id.description: Version id to restore, from list_config_versions. One of version_number/version_id is required.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason recorded in the audit trail.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for this rollback; repeating it returns the first outcome. Defaults to a key from the agent, the target version and the version live now, so rolling back to the same version again after later changes works. The result returns the key used.

actor.description: Do not set. Kept for older clients; the signed-in connection identifies you.

authority.description: Do not set. It cannot approve a change: the owner approves through review_url or by being signed in.

queue_for_approval.description: Create a durable owner-review request (default true). Setting false returns needs_approval, but an authority-envelope retry still cannot execute.

dry_run.description: Validate tenant, scope, and policy without touching the live config.

source_ref.description: External source reference, such as a ticket or automation run ID.

result.description: On executed: { agent_id, restored_from_version, restored_fields, skipped_fields, not_restored, new_version_number, warning? }.

tools.name: list_observability_events
tools.title: List Observability Events
tools.description: List a business-scoped timeline of compact call-runtime events and redacted integration-delivery attempts. Uses bounded keyset pagination.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the previous page.

tools.name: list_tool_execution_logs
tools.title: List Tool Execution Logs
tools.description: List per-call voice-agent tool execution traces — outcome, latency, timeout, and a redacted result preview for each routed tool call. Answers "did this tool call actually work".

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

outcome_status.description: Outcome envelope status filter (e.g. success, needs_clarification, unavailable, queued, retryable_delay, hard_failure).

tools.name: list_subscription_history
tools.title: List Subscription Change History
tools.description: List the business plan and price changes, newest first: upgrades, downgrades, add-ons and automatic right-size moves.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: list_overage_charges
tools.title: List Overage Charges
tools.description: List the per-period overage-minutes ledger (older per-minute-overage plans only; current plans carry no overage). GET /v1/balance/get_balance only returns an aggregate; this returns the underlying per-period ledger rows.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: list_rightsize_recommendations
tools.title: List Plan Right-Size Recommendations
tools.description: List per-period automatic plan right-size decisions, including the dry_run -> notified -> (kept | applied | superseded) lifecycle. Answers "is this business about to get right-sized".

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: get_billing_contacts
tools.title: Get Invoice Email Recipients
tools.description: Read who gets the monthly invoice email for a business. Every paid invoice is always emailed to the business owner (returned masked); up to 3 extra addresses, such as a bookkeeper or office inbox, get the same email.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

owner_email.description: The owner's login email, masked. The owner always gets every invoice.

tools.name: set_billing_contacts
tools.title: Set Invoice Email Recipients
tools.description: Replace the extra addresses that get the monthly invoice email (at most 3; an empty list clears them). The business owner always keeps getting every invoice and cannot be removed. Requires the current owner role on the business.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

emails.description: The full list of extra invoice email addresses. Replaces the current list; [] clears it.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.title: Get Subscription
tools.description: Read the business's own plan: no_paid_plan, active, or canceling, with the plan name and the renewal or end date. Use before cancel_subscription to tell the owner what will happen.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel Subscription
tools.description: Cancel the business's plan when the owner asks to. The plan stays on until the end of the paid period (or trial) and is never charged again; a past-due plan ends now. Pass undo=true to keep a plan whose cancel has not taken effect yet. Requires the current owner role. Confirm with the owner before calling.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

reason.description: Why the owner is cancelling. Required to cancel (not for undo): ask the owner, and pass other with their words in detail if none fits.

undo.description: true keeps the plan: undoes a cancel that has not taken effect yet.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.title: Report an Issue
tools.description: Report a problem with your KaiCalls agent, phone number, billing, or account. Saves the report to your change history and notifies KaiCalls support so a person can follow up on anything broken or not working as expected.

business_id.description: Business ID (optional only when the token can access exactly one business).

summary.description: One-line summary of the problem (max 200 characters).

description.description: Full details: what happened, what you expected, and any relevant call or time.

severity.description: How badly this is affecting the business.

category.description: What part of the product this issue relates to.

reporter_email.description: Email address support should reply to, if different from the account email.
